lines.text: Electric cars get a tiny five percent tax in India. Hybrids are crushed with forty-three percent. Yet hybrid bookings are surging.
In chaotic city traffic, regular cars burn fuel constantly. But a strong hybrid shuts its petrol engine off, gliding on electric power to deliver twenty-eight kilometers per liter.
No broken highway chargers, no range anxiety. One fuel tank gives over one thousand kilometers of real-world freedom. It refuels in two minutes flat.
While EV purists wait for charging networks, the hybrid quietly conquered the Indian road. Pragmatism beats ideology every single time.
